doc.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Warning young people off drugs and a sunny outlook
summary: He says fun is in friends and he has overcome adversity.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I’ve had – they’ve given me a lot too. I really have had a lot of fun. I try to – whatever – if I speak to young kids or people like that, I always tell them, don’t get involved with the narcotics things. Whatever you do, stay away from that. You try to call their attention to the fact that the fun they have is what they – is greatest when they’re having it with their schoolmates and things like that, the little things they laugh about, the little jokes they play – pranks they play on each other. That’s the joy of being what they are, not sticking a needle in your arms, smoking marijuana, or becoming a drunkard. That’s not it. That’s all detrimental and does nothing to enhance your life. It just tears you down. If they understand, as I say, that the fun is in what they’re doing with each other and that kind of a thing, they may relate to that and realize, because a lot of the fun I’ve had has been just on that basis alone.
You have a remarkably sunny view of the world and of your own – you are able to grab pleasure, it sounds like, from just about anything you do.
Yeah, and I’ve been fortunate. I’ve really been fortunate. I’ve overcome a lot of adversity. I’ve been able to do it. You look back and say, let’s not be mad with everybody, because here I am.
